newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 24.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Tuesday.
- Irish prime minister John Bruton and British premier Tony Blair have agreed a position on how to deal with the decommissioning of paramilitary weapons.
- Three senior Fianna Fail frontbench members are considered likely to be passed over when, as seems certain, Bertie Ahern is elected prime minister and names his cabinet on Thursday.
- A woman may have been part of the IRA gang which shot dead two police officers in Lurgan in Northern Ireland last Monday.

- IAWS, along with the venture capital group ACT, have emerged as the front-runners to put together a rescue package for Bell Lines in conjunction with senior members of the shipping company's management.
- John Bruton and Tony Blair have agreed a new approach to paramilitary arms decommissioning aimed at breaking the deadlock in the peace process.
- A police investigation is underway into two Dublin cab firms with suspected IRA and vigilante links.
- New figures show that Ireland's building societies last year lent 1.7 billion Irish pounds, an increase of 34 percent on 1995.
- Plans to phase out high food prices as a means of subsidising farm incomes are being prepared in a radical overhaul of the EU's 30 billion a year farm policy.

- Fianna Fail were last night predicting that Bertie Ahern would be elected prime minister of a new partnership government with the Progressive Democrats when parliament meets on Thursday. - IDA Ireland is creating more than 1,000 jobs a month as the Celtic Tiger shows no signs of losing momentum.
